matrix.description: malformed decision -> reject; 0 external effects
missing evidence -> INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
unauthorized human -> deny; 0 external effects
unauthorized agent -> tool/action unavailable or denied; 0 effects
matrix.note: Phase 9: the same property additionally proven live through the actual MCP tool surface (services/mcp), not just the raw decision_service HTTP API.

matrix.description: policy deny -> explanation recorded
approval required -> no execution before valid approval
invalid RDF transition -> transaction rejected
stale evidence -> reject/require refresh per policy
source identity ambiguous -> quarantine/typed failure; no guessing
duplicate API request -> same logical effect once
concurrent duplicate -> unique idempotency enforcement
worker crash pre-call -> resume safely
worker crash post-call/pre-record -> recover without duplicate effect
commit-then-timeout -> retry resolves via idempotency/reconciliation
200 without commit -> never observed_success
partial commit -> DIVERGED / compensation path
wrong quantity -> DIVERGED
matrix.note: Same observable shape as F16 (actual != requested quantity) from outcome_eval's predicate — one fault, one test, both IDs.

matrix.description: CDC delayed -> awaiting observation, then converge
CDC duplicated -> idempotent ingestion
CDC reordered -> no invariant break; version/order logic explicit
Kafka temporarily down -> backpressure/recovery, no fabricated freshness
matrix.note: Building this test found and fixed a real deadlock bug — see docs/experiment/implementation-notes.md Phase 6b section.

matrix.description: RDF4J temporarily down -> governed proposal fails safely
matrix.note: Unchanged behavior from Phase 5: RDF4J unreachable means no governed Decision could even be attempted (evidence-gathering/the SHACL-validated write itself fails) -- HTTP 503, zero Decision record written at all (proposal_attempt_failures logs the attempt). Distinct from F23/F24 below, where a Decision IS written (the OTHER gate already ran) but records the specific gate as unavailable.

matrix.description: OpenFGA unavailable -> fail closed for protected action
matrix.note: Phase 8 step 0 fix: an OpenFGA outage now yields the new terminal status GATE_UNAVAILABLE (unavailable_gate='authorization'), HTTP 503 on POST /decisions/propose -- never the previous DENIED_AUTHORIZATION, which fabricated a denial the gate never actually issued (acceptance criterion A.11). Still fully governed (a real, SHACL-validated Decision is written -- contracts/ontology/v3 + contracts/shapes/v3 add oo:GateUnavailable to the enumeration) and still fail-closed (0 effects, decision_content_hash never set). The test now also replays the resulting decision once OpenFGA recovers and asserts status == PASS_FAIL_CLOSED_VERIFIED (services/decision_service/replay.py's new replay class for exactly this case) -- never FAIL for not reproducing a resolved outage.

matrix.description: OPA unavailable -> fail closed unless action explicitly classified otherwise
matrix.note: Phase 8 step 0 fix: same treatment as F23 above, for the policy gate -- an OPA outage now yields GATE_UNAVAILABLE (unavailable_gate='policy'), HTTP 503, never the previous DENIED_POLICY. Replays as PASS_FAIL_CLOSED_VERIFIED once OPA recovers.

matrix.description: Temporal unavailable -> approved decision remains unexecuted, auditable
hot projection stale -> freshness visible; policy may reject
projection corrupt -> consistency check detects mismatch
ontology migration incompatible -> CI/replay build fails
matrix.note: scripts/compat_check.py (Makefile `test-contracts`) fails a published contracts/<kind>/vN (N>=2) that lacks migration coverage. Positive case: the real repo tree has zero violations. Negative cases: a synthetic version with no migrations/ dir, an empty migrations/ dir, and a migration.json pointing at a nonexistent script are all caught.

matrix.description: old policy deleted -> replay fails loudly; experiment considered failed
matrix.note: services/decision_service/replay.py::_verify_archive re-hashes every archived contract directory a decision pinned before re-running any gate; a deleted or modified archived policy file raises ReplayIntegrityError (HTTP 409 via POST /replay/{id}) -- verified live against a real V1 corpus decision, restored, and re-verified PASS again.

matrix.description: prompt injection -> no policy bypass
matrix.note: Implemented this phase: services/mcp (the MCP agent surface) + a deterministic scripted 'compromised planner' (tests/agent/) that IS spec 09's prompt-injection scenario, driven live against the real MCP tool surface — the architectural property (H9: 'even a fully compromised planner cannot bypass enforcement') holds regardless of whether the request came from a jailbroken LLM prompt or a scripted client, since decision_service re-runs every gate server-side either way. A 500-unit request lands REQUIRES_APPROVAL (never auto-allow), and a follow-up attempt to execute it anyway is rejected (409), zero WMS effects, verified against real ground truth.

matrix.description: action definition changes post-approval -> approved pinned version executes or decision invalidated explicitly
matrix.note: Newly IMPLEMENTED this phase, not just tested: oo:actionPinnedSha256 stamped at propose(), re-verified fresh off disk at execute() time (services/action_worker/activities.py::verify_and_start_execution). New oo:ActionVersionInvalidated status (contracts/ontology/v1/oo-core.ttl, contracts/shapes/v1/decision-shape.ttl).

matrix.description: clock skew -> ordering relies on source offsets/IDs where required, not wall clock alone
matrix.note: services/ingestion/lsn.py takes no wall-clock input at all — the F20 reordering test already exercises the same LSN-based ordering property; these two are dedicated unit + component proofs framed explicitly around clock skew, per the brief's own 'or document why F20 covers it and add a unit test' option.

matrix.description: unrelated concurrent stock receipt -> reconciliation recognizes intended transfer correctly
source DB direct manual edit -> observed as external fact with provenance, not retroactively attributed to action
event poison message -> DLQ/quarantine; pipeline health visible
matrix.note: The DLQ mechanism itself (services/ingestion/consumer.py::send_to_dlq) shipped in Phase 3; this phase adds the first live end-to-end test driving it via a real malformed Kafka message.

matrix.description: invalid mapping rule deployment -> compatibility fixture catches or ambiguity exposed
matrix.note: services/identity_resolver/resolver.py::IdentityResolver already validated mapping_rules.yaml at load time (ConflictingMappingRuleError, explicitly commented "F39") since an earlier phase -- this phase is the first to exercise it: conflicting explicit-override entries, an unknown rule kind, and a pattern rule missing canonical_template are all caught loudly at load time; a known-negative (structurally valid file) still loads and resolves correctly.

matrix.description: trace/log unavailable -> business correctness survives; canonical provenance remains in data model
matrix.note: Implemented this phase (docs/experiment/briefs/phase10a.md item 5): a minimal OpenTelemetry pipeline (an otel-collector service exporting to a file, services/decision_service's propose/approve/execute spans carrying decision_id/action_execution_id/actor_id/trace_id — see services/common/tracing.py) makes traces-reference.txt point at real trace data (scripts/gen_traces_reference.py). F40 itself: the otel-collector container is stopped entirely and a full propose->approve->execute cycle is driven through the real decision_service HTTP API, asserting every step succeeds exactly as it would with tracing available. Canonical provenance (decision_id/action_execution_id in the response body, the governed Decision record itself) was never sourced from tracing in the first place, so it is provably unaffected — only the best-effort trace export is impacted, and it degrades silently (services/common/tracing.py's own docstring: only span setup/teardown failures are swallowed, and the BatchSpanProcessor's export happens on a background thread decoupled from the request path, so a dead collector adds no latency to any real request).
